details.description: Qwen3-4B is a 4-billion-parameter dense chat model from Alibaba's Qwen team, released April 29, 2025 as part of the Qwen3 family. It can switch between an extended 'thinking' mode for step-by-step reasoning and a fast 'non-thinking' mode within a single model, toggled via the enable_thinking parameter or /think and /no_think chat commands. Its native context window is 32,768 tokens, extendable to 131,072 tokens using YaRN rope scaling; Fireworks AI, which serves this model, lists a 40.9K-token context limit instead. Qwen's model card states the model surpasses the earlier QwQ and Qwen2.5-Instruct models on mathematics, code generation and reasoning tasks.
advantages: Qwen's model card states the model surpasses the earlier QwQ and Qwen2.5-Instruct models on mathematics, code generation, and commonsense reasoning tasks.
Supports switching between thinking and non-thinking modes within one model, via the enable_thinking parameter or /think and /no_think chat commands, per the model card.
Supports tool calling, including MCP configurations and built-in tools, per the model card.
Qwen's Qwen3 announcement blog states the Qwen3 family supports 119 languages and dialects.
disadvantages: Native context window is 32,768 tokens; extending to 131,072 tokens requires YaRN rope scaling, which the model card says can degrade performance on shorter texts if enabled unnecessarily.
The model card warns against greedy decoding in thinking mode, saying it can lead to performance degradation and endless repetitions.
use_cases: General-purpose dialogue and quick-response chat via non-thinking mode
Math, coding and logical-reasoning tasks via thinking mode, per the model card
Tool calling and MCP-based agent tasks, per the model card
Lightweight deployment where a smaller dense model than Qwen3-32B is preferred

notes: Catalog's 40,960 max input/output tokens match Fireworks' own listed 40.9K-token context limit for this model on that host; Qwen's model card states a native context of 32,768 tokens, extendable to 131,072 tokens with YaRN scaling. No numeric benchmark table for this exact checkpoint was found on the maker's own pages, so evaluations is left empty rather than guessed.
